results.summary: This Wokwi project drives a display to draw the letter H when all input switches are turned on. It is a simple combinational design with eight inputs and eight outputs, tested by flipping the switches and observing the letter. No external hardware is specified beyond the default simulation environment. The documentation is minimal and does not describe the internal logic or any silicon results.

This project implements a full adder using three inputs: two data bits and a carry-in, with outputs for sum and carry-out. It is tested by applying input combinations and observing the two output bits, optionally with an LED. The design is a basic educational exercise in digital arithmetic. No silicon results or further implementation details are provided.

This design uses OR gates to generate the letter J on a seven-segment LED display. It is controlled by eight input switches and produces eight outputs, tested by flipping switches to form the letter. The project relies on the default seven-segment display and switches in the Wokwi simulator. The documentation is sparse and does not explain the exact gate arrangement or any hardware results.

This project combines a half adder and a NOT gate, with two inputs feeding the adder and one input feeding the inverter, while other inputs pass through. It is tested by flipping switches to light up a clock display. The design requires the default seven-segment display and DIP switches. The documentation is brief and does not provide detailed schematics or silicon results.

This is a half adder built from an XOR gate for the sum and an AND gate for the carry. It uses two inputs and provides sum and carry outputs, tested by changing inputs and observing LED indicators. Two LED displays are needed to see the outputs. The project is a straightforward educational logic exercise with minimal documentation.

This design is a three-bit binary counter that displays its count from 0 to 7 on a seven-segment display. It uses three input pins to set the binary value and drives the seven segments plus a dot output. Testing involves setting the input pins and observing the corresponding digit. The project requires a segment display and an eight-pin switch, and is a basic educational counter with limited documentation.

This project implements an 8-to-3 encoder using a single AND gate and a single OR gate. It is tested by activating inputs, with inputs 6 and 7 sharing an OR gate so only one should be on at a time; correct operation outputs the number 8 with a dot. No external hardware is required. The documentation is brief and does not detail the full truth table or silicon results.

This project turns on blue and purple LEDs based on switch inputs. It is tested by turning on a switch in the corner of the simulation. An external LED light is listed as required hardware. The documentation is very thin and does not explain the internal logic or any specific function beyond lighting LEDs.

This project is described as an XAND gate, using inputs and outputs. It is tested by running the simulation. External logic gates are mentioned as hardware, though the description is unclear. The documentation is extremely sparse and does not explain the gate's function or provide any test results.

This design contains four inverters, with four inputs directly connected to outputs and the remaining inputs inverted. It is tested by toggling inputs and observing the outputs. No external hardware is required. The documentation is minimal and does not provide a schematic or silicon results.
